title: How this project was driven
note: Human-directed, agent-built. Dates are UTC. No verbatim prompts, no personal data. Actors: human (project owner), planner (reviewing agent), builder (build lead agent), subagent (delegated task agent).

entries.summary: Asked for a neutral study of the WebMCP specification, Chrome documentation, ChatGPT site tools, the showcase, and the challenge rules before choosing a product.
entries.outcome: The research established the API contract, browser differences, secure-context needs, and submission constraints.

entries.summary: Proposed a live meeting architecture whiteboard and asked for a critical assessment.
entries.outcome: The idea was rejected because it overlapped existing whiteboards and did not need WebMCP. The pointing and shared-selection insight was kept.

entries.summary: Ran an adversarial comparison of about fifteen candidates against the official judging criteria.
entries.outcome: Generic dashboards and cross-site workflows were removed. The chosen product had to depend on live unsaved page state and page-owned deterministic actions.

entries.summary: Checked a manufacturing containment review against practitioner needs and existing products.
entries.outcome: The concept was narrowed and kept only as a fallback because its three-minute story was harder to explain.

entries.summary: Chose a restaurant ordering exception workflow for a clearer demo and a broader audience.
entries.outcome: The live-state pattern moved to a supplier order sheet where signals, pins, preview, adoption, and receipt are visible together.

entries.summary: Re-read the rules and WebMCP documentation, computed the deterministic data, and wrote the build brief and review checklist.
entries.outcome: Cutoff, its five tools, the ten-line data set, the expected totals, and the three review checkpoints were locked.

entries.summary: Wrote failing tests first, then implemented the seed data, pure order engine, revisioned store, and thin WebMCP adapters.
entries.outcome: The engine reproduced the exact table. Stale writes, preview invalidation, adoption, undo, receipt storage, and registration lifecycle passed deterministic tests.

entries.summary: Clarified that checkpoint times define order rather than deadlines and added official model-backed evals to the preview stage.
entries.outcome: Quality gates stayed intact. Static evals measure the required first read, while browser evals measure full ordered chains against live state.

entries.summary: Ran Review 1 tests and the locked flow over local HTTPS in system Chrome and the in-app browser.
entries.outcome: The exact 910-cover, 76-hour, 2,767-unit preview passed. Tool registration changed from four tools to five during preview and returned to four after adoption.

entries.summary: Passed Review 1 and found one state-lifecycle defect plus small annotation, date-copy, and artifact-hygiene issues.
entries.outcome: Row focus became view-only, tool annotations now match their outputs, fixed dates are explicit, and generated browser artifacts are ignored.

entries.summary: Completed the styled order sheet, all eight panels, keyboard controls, receipt actions, activity log, trajectory route, and storage hardening.
entries.outcome: The security review found no high-severity issue. Storage bounds and exception handling gained regression coverage.

entries.summary: Ran the preview flow, independent agent trials, the official eval suites, and the available audit command.
entries.outcome: Sonnet passed 8 of 8 first calls and 17 of 17 browser steps. Gemini 3.7 Flash passed 8 of 8 first calls. A clean Sol run completed the full tool flow. Failed zero-score attempts remain recorded. Ora stopped before scoring because its current CLI and service use different capture versions.

entries.summary: Repeated the deployed flow by hand and passed Review 2 for the builder-owned work. The review found two small product gaps.
entries.outcome: The signal form now explains an empty label. Managers can create the same local handoff receipt through visible controls or the agent tool.

entries.summary: Prepared the local Review 3 package and verified the two Review 2 fixes before updating the preview.
entries.outcome: All 43 tests and the production build passed. The README, timed demo plan, Devpost draft, changelog, trajectory, and MIT license are ready for the final external checks.

entries.summary: Traced a human Chrome inspector failure after successful adoption to immediate dynamic-tool unregistration.
entries.outcome: The adapter now returns the adoption result before unregistering the tool. A regression test covers the ordering, all 43 tests pass, and the corrected preview is live.

entries.summary: Accepted the external Gemini outage after reviewing the combined Chrome, in-app browser, Sonnet, gateway Gemini, and inspector evidence.
entries.outcome: Review 2 closed without more manual retries. Review 3 moved to the public repository and submission-package checks.

entries.summary: Published the audited package to the approved public repository and checked the live GitHub record.
entries.outcome: The default branch is main, GitHub recognizes the MIT license, local and remote commits match, and private build references are absent.

entries.summary: Deployed the approved production build and repeated the locked flow on the canonical URL in both required browsers.
entries.outcome: The live bundle matches the verified local build. WebMCP moved from four tools to five and back to four around the exact preview and adoption. After correcting one factually inconsistent handoff fixture, the production browser eval passed 17 of 17 steps.

entries.summary: Applied the final legibility, accessibility, tool-contract, and trust review, then cross-checked production with current model families and two public auditors.
entries.outcome: All 47 tests passed. Direct tool calls and browser-driven page actions now carry truthful interaction channels. Four models passed the first-call suite, three models exercised live browser chains, and Ora scored Shared Experience, Tool Quality, and Trust at 100.

entries.summary: Approved the staged expansion from one order review into a four-section shift operations desk, with a review after each stage.
entries.outcome: Stage 0 was limited to the shared shell, navigation, route-scoped tools, and the identified order-page interaction fixes. Decision pages remain gated behind later reviews.

entries.summary: Built the Stage 0 shell and wrote failing behavior and registration tests before changing runtime code.
entries.outcome: One revisioned store now spans four routes. Human inputs refresh active previews or surface pending work, line math separates calculation from a pin, and route changes replace the registered tool set. The accessibility pass closed its concrete keyboard and validation findings. All 55 tests and the production build pass locally.

entries.summary: Published the authorized Stage 0 build to a non-production Vercel Preview and repeated route, interaction, and registration checks on the deployed artifact.
entries.outcome: All five public routes returned 200 with preview indexing disabled. Chrome preserved the shared revision through navigation with no console errors, while the in-app browser exposed six tools on Order and only open_section on Stock. The production deployment was not changed.

entries.summary: Built the Stock count sheet and waste ledger as the first shared decision page after Order.
entries.outcome: Live counts and waste now feed the order engine through one revisioned store. The locked waste totals, count effects, lettuce waste result, and stale-preview behavior pass deterministic tests. Stock exposes three focused tools plus section navigation.

entries.summary: Self-reviewed Stage 1 across deterministic tests, both page widths, route-scoped tools, cross-page invalidation, accessibility, and model-backed evals.
entries.outcome: All 68 tests pass. The Stock browser suite passed five of five steps, the first-call suite passed thirteen of thirteen cases, and the final non-production preview is live. Production was not changed.

entries.summary: Stopped after the Stage 1 self-review because the next stages depend on product decisions that are not present in the expansion materials.
entries.outcome: The Stage 2 roster and deterministic suggestion outcomes, and the Stage 3 rainy-Tuesday numbers, are assigned to separate addenda in the brief. No values were invented.

entries.summary: Resumed with the approved Labor addendum and built roster planning as the third decision page.
entries.outcome: Labor now reads the adopted order, records absences and extra shifts, proposes deterministic releases and on-call cover, and keeps adoption reversible. The corrected 830-cover split is 25 lunch, 34 dinner, and 11 prep.

entries.summary: Self-reviewed Labor across exact engine assertions, shared-state invalidation, responsive UI, accessibility, route tools, and model selection.
entries.outcome: All 83 tests passed at the Stage 2 boundary. The final Labor browser chain passed eight of eight steps, and safe prerequisite reads remained visible in the multi-model first-call record.

entries.summary: Completed the four-section desk with Shift log, service-day presets, and local exports.
entries.outcome: Shift log reuses the shared activity and receipts, accepts bounded notes, and downloads filtered JSON. Order downloads the working plan as CSV. Saturday and rainy Tuesday share the same engines but have independent deterministic seeds.

entries.summary: Ran the Stage 3 deterministic suite and current-model first-call cross-check before the final browser and release gates.
entries.outcome: All 102 tests and the production build passed. Three model families scored nineteen of nineteen first calls; Sonnet made the correct Labor read plus one extra safe read, recorded as eighteen of nineteen. The CSV total follows the authoritative rows, which sum to 78 rather than the addendum's inconsistent 71.

entries.summary: Closed the final accessibility and security review, then repeated the full local browser ladder through Portless HTTPS.
entries.outcome: Visible controls and tool adapters now share the same bounds, read-only tools preserve state, Tuesday receipts restore to Tuesday, order controls announce completion, and Vercel has basic response hardening. Chrome completed both service-day flows at desktop and mobile widths. A final browser finding kept open_section registered across asynchronous route cleanup, and both browsers then reported exact tool sets without a registration warning.

entries.summary: Stress-tested the corrected route-registration lifecycle on the final non-production preview before release.
entries.outcome: Fifty rapid transitions produced exact route tool sets in every immediate and next-task observation. The shared navigation tool was never absent, registration errors stayed at zero, the full Saturday and Tuesday flow passed, and the in-app browser independently reported the expected tool sets.

entries.summary: Deployed the four-section desk to the canonical production URL and ran the expanded live browser suite once.
entries.outcome: All routes returned 200 with the expected response headers. Chrome completed the full Saturday and Tuesday flow and 50 rapid route transitions without a registration gap. The model completed all 21 eval tasks; two of 48 strict matcher steps recorded an extra safe Stock read.

entries.summary: Ran one fresh production scan through Ora's dedicated WebMCP audit with a natural restaurant-shift goal.
entries.outcome: Ora captured all six Order tools and scored Shared Experience 100, Task Completion 47, Tool Quality 99, and Trust 100. Its generic task grader still used document-editor intents, and its live agent received only the two read tools. The result is recorded without changing the product to satisfy those mismatched checks.

entries.summary: Reduced the public evaluation package to the evidence a reviewer needs.
entries.outcome: Generated browser-eval reports now stay in the ignored local workspace. Public files retain the fixtures, exact scores, model names, failure analysis, and auditor results without repetitive raw trajectories.

entries.summary: Reviewed every finding in Ora's current six-tool production report before reviewer handoff.
entries.outcome: Shared Experience and Trust have no open warning. The Task Completion grader used document-editor actions and its custom live runner withheld four tools that the capture recorded. Ora's only quality warning says open_section lacks a verb while proposing the same name as its fix. No product contract changed for those mismatches.

entries.summary: Applied the two copy changes from the final review.
entries.outcome: The header describes the full operations desk. Shift-log summaries name staff and omit generated order and labor preview identifiers, while structured tool results retain those identifiers for safe follow-up calls.

entries.summary: Applied a locked legibility pass without changing engines, state transitions, tools, schemas, or evaluation fixtures.
entries.outcome: All four decision pages now share one live service band for covers, labor, order cost, waste, and exceptions. The header establishes the service day, and Labor compares required and scheduled hours with compact bars and signed variance.

entries.summary: Verified the legibility pass across deterministic tests, production build output, desktop and mobile captures, and a non-production deployment.
entries.outcome: All 108 current tests passed. Eight route screenshots cover 1,280 px and 390 px, the preview serves every route with the expected headers, and the deployed Order page exposes its six WebMCP tools. Production was left unchanged for review.

entries.summary: Conditionally passed the Stage 4 layout and found two data-basis defects in the shared band during an active order preview.
entries.outcome: The preview total used a stale event breakdown, and labor exceptions used preview demand while the Labor tile described the working order. The review also requested explicit preview labels for proposed covers and cost.

entries.summary: Separated proposed order values from the working-order labor basis and repeated the cancelled-event preview flow.
entries.outcome: The band now shows preview 830 as base 830 plus zero derby covers, marks the cancellation, labels the proposed 2,437-unit cost, and keeps Labor at required 95 with gap zero until adoption. Only the expiring-stock exception remains. All 109 tests and the build pass.

entries.summary: Extended the Stage 4 check through adoption and found that the working-order breakdown restored the seed event uplift.
entries.outcome: The displayed 910 covers incorrectly sat beside base 830, derby 310, and bookings 80. The engine result was correct; only the band used the wrong source after adoption.

entries.summary: Made the band use the order engine's active-event and pinned-booking selectors in preview and working states.
entries.outcome: The regression now covers preview and adoption. After adoption, 910 covers resolve to base 830, zero active derby covers, and 80 pinned booking covers. Labor shows required 76 with gap plus 19, with Lunch and Dinner alerts. All 109 tests and the build pass.

entries.summary: Checked Undo and found that retained signals no longer described the restored saved order.
entries.outcome: After Undo, the working order returned to 1,140 covers while the retained cancellation and booking still summed to 910. The tile needed an invariant rather than another state branch.

entries.summary: Made the Covers tile print arithmetic only when its terms equal the displayed total, then reviewed every service-band data source.
entries.outcome: Undo and other unmatched states now say that recorded signals are not in the working order. Seed, preview, and adopted states keep their exact arithmetic. Labor, order cost, waste, and attention each use one consistent basis. All 109 tests and the build pass.

entries.summary: Approved Review 4 after the preview, adoption, and Undo states used consistent service-band data.
entries.outcome: The approved build became the production candidate. No further product or contract changes were requested before the video.

entries.summary: Deployed the approved build and refreshed the submission screenshots from the canonical production domain.
entries.outcome: Five 1,440 by 900 production captures now cover the seed desk, order preview, labor preview, stock reconciliation, and filtered shift log. Each image was inspected before the release commit.

entries.summary: Requested a readability correction after checking the production desk at normal laptop zoom.
entries.outcome: The next candidate must fit the viewport width, raise the text floor, make the first Order step visible, clarify navigation, and adopt a higher-contrast dashboard palette without changing product behavior.

entries.summary: Applied and checked the Stage 4B presentation-only candidate through the canonical local HTTPS route.
entries.outcome: All five routes have a 12-pixel text floor at desktop and mobile widths. The four decision pages have no root mobile overflow, the first Order step is visible at laptop height, and eight route screenshots record the responsive dashboard treatment. Production remains unchanged for review.
